findings.evidence: `Covariance.lean:126-128` has `i < j → k < l`; Mathlib provides `ProbabilityTheory.covariance_comm` at `mathlib/Mathlib/Probability/Moments/Covariance.lean:75`, so reversed off-diagonal pairs need no extra contractability.
findings.fix: State/prove a public `Contractable.covariance_eq_of_ne` with hypotheses `i ≠ j` and `k ≠ l`, using `lt_or_gt_of_ne` plus `ProbabilityTheory.covariance_comm`, and derive the `<` version only as a specialization if desired.
findings.issue: `Contractable.covariance_eq_of_lt` only handles `i < j` and `k < l`, but the natural covariance-structure statement is for all off-diagonal pairs `i ≠ j` and `k ≠ l`; reversed pairs are covered by `covariance_comm`.

findings.evidence: `Covariance.lean:143-144` packages `(∀ i j k l, i < j → k < l → ...)`, while the docstring at lines 137-139 describes a single common off-diagonal covariance.
findings.fix: Change the third component to `∀ i j k l, i ≠ j → k ≠ l → cov[X i, X j; μ] = cov[X k, X l; μ]`, backed by the generalized covariance lemma.
findings.issue: `contractable_covariance_structure` packages the same under-generalized covariance field, requiring both pairs to be increasing rather than merely off-diagonal.

summary: The covariance API is under-generalized: it exposes only increasing index pairs even though covariance symmetry gives the natural off-diagonal statement.
